title: Discrete-time generalized canonical transformations for non-autonomous systems
summary: A dynamical system is said to be \emph{non-autonomous} when the differential equations describing its evolution depends explicitly on time. Among the various geometric approaches to investigate such systems, the cosymplectic formulation provides a natural framework that extends symplectic geometry to time-dependent Hamiltonians systems. However, preserving the associated geometric structures under numerical discretization remains a challenging problem: standard integrators, such as explicit Euler schemes, generally fail to conserve the cosymplectic volume or the underlying Poisson structure.…
